**Digne-les-Bains** (French pronunciation:[[diɲ le bɛ̃]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")ⓘ; Occitan: _Dinha dei Banhs_), or simply and historically **Digne** (_Dinha_ in the classical norm or _Digno_ in the Mistralian norm), is the prefecture of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provencedepartment in the [Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provence-Alpes-C%C3%B4te_d'Azur "Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur")region of southern France. Its inhabitants are called _Dignois_ (masculine) and _Dignoises_ (feminine).
Digne-les-Bains and neighboring municipalities
Located on the edge of the Digne Prealps and on both sides of the river Bléone, which flows southwest through the middle of the commune and crosses the town; it forms part of the commune's northeastern and southwestern borders.
Digne-les-Bains is the capital of the Department of Alpes de Haute-Provence. Placed in the geographical centre of the Department, the commune is home to 17,400 inhabitants, making it one of the smaller prefectures of France by its population. The town centre is at 608 metres (1,995 ft) altitude.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-LaTorre-3)

Digne is a sprawling commune in the plain formed around the Bléone Valley, given that the terrain that surrounds it is very rugged. The old town is built on a hill between the Bléone and the torrent of the hot springs, but the town has gradually extended in the three directions of the valleys, especially downstream. Its geographical location is quite remarkable, given that it lies at the edge of the Prealps, on a thrust fault that bears its name. A part of the town is completely enclosed in the Bléone Valley, while the town extends widely, on a gentler relief, downstream. With the annexation of neighbouring towns, especially downstream, the town extends over 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) in length.

### Neighbouring communes
[edit]
The communes surrounding Digne-les-Bains are La Robine-sur-Galabre, Le Brusquet, Marcoux, Archail, Tartonne, Clumanc, Chaudon-Norante, Châteauredon, Le Chaffaut-Saint-Jurson, Aiglun, Champtercier and Thoard.
Digne-les-Bains features a mid-latitude humid subtropical climate (Köppen climate classification: _Cfa_), with mediterranean (_Csa_) and oceanic (_Cfb_) influences. Summers are hot and relatively dry, and winters are mildly cold and relatively wet, with air frosts being regular in the winter months.

### Geology and terrain
[edit]
The commune, which is at the heart of the geology, has its specificities related to the ancient town _[clarification needed_] built upstream of the cluse which the Bléone has worn into the _Nappe de Digne_ to emerge into the tertiary basin of Valensole.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5)
The districts of the town cover the alluvium of the streams which converge upstream of the Cluse. The most eastern suburbs joined a line of limestone hills with flint of the Carixian age, forming russet cliffs oriented to the south-west.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5) The hot springs were captured, since ancient times, to the point where these carixian limestones are cut by the hack of the southernmost valley, descending from Entrages. Their healing powers are linked to their ascent along the gypsiferous Triassic levels of the sole thrust of the _Nappe de Digne_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5)
The most visible mountain of the commune is Le Cousson at 1,516 metres (4,974 ft); the Bigué rises to 1,653 metres (5,423 ft).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Brunet1-6)

## Population and society
### Area and population
*   Fourteen schools, 11 primary schools, a private primary school (under contract and whose teachers are employees of National Education), and two nursery schools[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-79)  
*   The Maria-Borrely and Pierre-Gassendi collèges[fr][[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-80)  
*   Three lycées, including the Lycée professionnel Beau-de-Rochas,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-81) the Pierre-Gilles-de-Gennes[fr] and the multipurpose Alexandra-David-Neel[fr] school,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-82) which offers also two BTS certificates and further training of local initiative  
*   A University Institute of Technology, which provides lessons in agronomy, DUT engineering of the environment, DUT administrative and commercial management, DUT quality industrial logistics and organization, business tourism, geomatics professional license[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-83)

Digne was elected as the Sportiest town in France[fr] among towns with less than 20,000 inhabitants in 2006, by the daily newspaper _[L'Équipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'%C3%89quipe "L'Équipe")_.

## Population and society
### Area and population
The town has several sports facilities, with free access or reserved for the many sporting clubs and schools. These include gyms, a stadium, an equestrian centre, a golf course, and a public swimming pool. It is one of the rare French towns to provide free access to tennis courts.
At the request of the Junior Town Council, a skatepark has been renovated which is open access.
The town's hospitals have 480 beds.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Brunet1-6)
The following units have held garrison in Digne:
*   [22nd light infantry regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_r%C3%A9giment_d'infanterie?action=edit&redlink=1 "97th régiment d'infanterie (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/97e%20r%C3%A9giment%20d'infanterie "fr:97e régiment d'infanterie")] (one battalion in the middle of the 19th century);  
*   [3rd infantry regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3rd_r%C3%A9giment_d'infanterie_(France)?action=edit&redlink=1 "3rd régiment d'infanterie (France) (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/3e%20r%C3%A9giment%20d'infanterie%20(France) "fr:3e régiment d'infanterie (France)")]

## Population and society
### Area and population
Currently, several gendarmerie units are based in Digne. In addition to the capital of community brigade,[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-84) there is a motorised brigade, a [platoon of monitoring and intervention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peloton_de_surveillance_et_d'intervention_de_la_Gendarmerie?action=edit&redlink=1 "Peloton de surveillance et d'intervention de la Gendarmerie (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peloton%20de%20surveillance%20et%20d'intervention%20de%20la%20Gendarmerie "fr:Peloton de surveillance et d'intervention de la Gendarmerie")] (PSIG) and a squadron of Mobile Gendarmerie.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-85)
For Catholic worship, the city is the seat of the departmental bishopric, and therefore the Diocese of Digne, Riez and Sisteron. The bishop is Monsignor Jean-Philippe Nault[fr]. He was appointed in 2014 and is the youngest Bishop of France (born in 1965)._[citation needed_] The Catholic faithful have two places of worship for Mass: Notre-Dame-du-Bourg[fr] and Saint-Jérôme. The members of the Muslim faith also have their place of worship,[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-86) as well as Protestants[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-87) and Evangelicals.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-88)

**Digne-les-Bains**, or simply and historically Digne, is the prefecture of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department in the **Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur** region of Southeastern **France** on the **Bléone river**.
**Tourism and main attractions**
Digne Cathedral is a Roman Catholic church. The cathedral has been a monument historique since 1906. It is the seat of the Bishops of Digne, Riez and **Sisteron**, formerly Bishops of Digne.
Construction began in 1490 by the order of the then bishop Antoine de Guiramand to cater for the movement of the town’s population to a higher, more secure and defensible location round the local castle. The cathedral was renovated and expanded in the 1860s under the direction of architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly.
The previous cathedral in the old town, Notre-Dame-du-Bourg (Cathédrale Notre-Dame-du-Bourg de Digne), a late Romanesque building of the 13th century, still stands as a museum.
The Saint-Jérôme de Digne Cathedral is the second cathedral in the city. Located in the heart of the city, on the Rochas hill, from the 16th century it replaced the original episcopal seat located at Notre-Dame-du-Bourg.
Antoine de Guiramand, bishop of Digne, from 1479, was behind the construction of Saint-Jérôme cathedral. The building, erected from 1490 to 1500, is the work of Antoine Brollion, master mason in Barcelonnette. Originally, it had a central nave of four bays flanked by side aisles onto which chapels were added during the 17th century.
The Notre-Dame-de-Lourdes Church was built in 1870 on the Mountain of the Cross, north of Digne, though at the bottom of the slope. The brick walls are its main feature, with its large size.
The chapel of Saint-Vincent belonged to an abbey or priory. It is still in good condition. The Chapel of the Cross, located nearby, is gradually becoming a ruin.

The remains of fortifications can be recognised if one pays attention to the plan of the old town around the central district, built on the heights. Some of the walls and some towers which surrounded the city from the 14th century can still be seen. These remains of ramparts are currently based in the landscape of the dwellings.
The town of Digne was immortalized by Victor Hugo who placed the beginning of his famous novel Les Misérables there.
Museum of the Haute-Provence geological reserve and its butterfly garden.
Gassendi Museum with modern museography allowing the public to move from art to science, from ancient to contemporary through a journey through time. Its archeology section was founded in 1889.
World War II Museum. Documents and period objects evoke the strategic role of Digne-les-Bains in Alpine defense.
Alexandra David-Néel Museum, located in her house.

**Digne-les-Bains** (French pronunciation:[[diɲ le bɛ̃]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")ⓘ; Occitan: _Dinha dei Banhs_), or simply and historically **Digne** (_Dinha_ in the classical norm or _Digno_ in the Mistralian norm), is the prefecture of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provencedepartment in the [Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provence-Alpes-C%C3%B4te_d'Azur "Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur")region of southern France. Its inhabitants are called _Dignois_ (masculine) and _Dignoises_ (feminine).
Digne-les-Bains and neighboring municipalities
Located on the edge of the Digne Prealps and on both sides of the river Bléone, which flows southwest through the middle of the commune and crosses the town; it forms part of the commune's northeastern and southwestern borders.
Digne-les-Bains is the capital of the Department of Alpes de Haute-Provence. Placed in the geographical centre of the Department, the commune is home to 17,400 inhabitants, making it one of the smaller prefectures of France by its population. The town centre is at 608 metres (1,995 ft) altitude.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-LaTorre-3)
texts.2:
Digne is a sprawling commune in the plain formed around the Bléone Valley, given that the terrain that surrounds it is very rugged. The old town is built on a hill between the Bléone and the torrent of the hot springs, but the town has gradually extended in the three directions of the valleys, especially downstream. Its geographical location is quite remarkable, given that it lies at the edge of the Prealps, on a thrust fault that bears its name. A part of the town is completely enclosed in the Bléone Valley, while the town extends widely, on a gentler relief, downstream. With the annexation of neighbouring towns, especially downstream, the town extends over 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) in length.

The communes surrounding Digne-les-Bains are La Robine-sur-Galabre, Le Brusquet, Marcoux, Archail, Tartonne, Clumanc, Chaudon-Norante, Châteauredon, Le Chaffaut-Saint-Jurson, Aiglun, Champtercier and Thoard.
Digne-les-Bains features a mid-latitude humid subtropical climate (Köppen climate classification: _Cfa_), with mediterranean (_Csa_) and oceanic (_Cfb_) influences. Summers are hot and relatively dry, and winters are mildly cold and relatively wet, with air frosts being regular in the winter months.

### Geology and terrain
[edit]
The commune, which is at the heart of the geology, has its specificities related to the ancient town _[clarification needed_] built upstream of the cluse which the Bléone has worn into the _Nappe de Digne_ to emerge into the tertiary basin of Valensole.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5)
The districts of the town cover the alluvium of the streams which converge upstream of the Cluse. The most eastern suburbs joined a line of limestone hills with flint of the Carixian age, forming russet cliffs oriented to the south-west.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5) The hot springs were captured, since ancient times, to the point where these carixian limestones are cut by the hack of the southernmost valley, descending from Entrages. Their healing powers are linked to their ascent along the gypsiferous Triassic levels of the sole thrust of the _Nappe de Digne_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5)
The most visible mountain of the commune is Le Cousson at 1,516 metres (4,974 ft); the Bigué rises to 1,653 metres (5,423 ft).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Brunet1-6)

**Digne-les-Bains**, or simply and historically Digne, is the prefecture of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department in the **Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur** region of Southeastern **France** on the **Bléone river**.
**Tourism and main attractions**
Digne Cathedral is a Roman Catholic church. The cathedral has been a monument historique since 1906. It is the seat of the Bishops of Digne, Riez and **Sisteron**, formerly Bishops of Digne.
Construction began in 1490 by the order of the then bishop Antoine de Guiramand to cater for the movement of the town’s population to a higher, more secure and defensible location round the local castle. The cathedral was renovated and expanded in the 1860s under the direction of architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly.
The previous cathedral in the old town, Notre-Dame-du-Bourg (Cathédrale Notre-Dame-du-Bourg de Digne), a late Romanesque building of the 13th century, still stands as a museum.
The Saint-Jérôme de Digne Cathedral is the second cathedral in the city. Located in the heart of the city, on the Rochas hill, from the 16th century it replaced the original episcopal seat located at Notre-Dame-du-Bourg.
Antoine de Guiramand, bishop of Digne, from 1479, was behind the construction of Saint-Jérôme cathedral. The building, erected from 1490 to 1500, is the work of Antoine Brollion, master mason in Barcelonnette. Originally, it had a central nave of four bays flanked by side aisles onto which chapels were added during the 17th century.
The Notre-Dame-de-Lourdes Church was built in 1870 on the Mountain of the Cross, north of Digne, though at the bottom of the slope. The brick walls are its main feature, with its large size.
The chapel of Saint-Vincent belonged to an abbey or priory. It is still in good condition. The Chapel of the Cross, located nearby, is gradually becoming a ruin.
texts.1:
The remains of fortifications can be recognised if one pays attention to the plan of the old town around the central district, built on the heights. Some of the walls and some towers which surrounded the city from the 14th century can still be seen. These remains of ramparts are currently based in the landscape of the dwellings.
The town of Digne was immortalized by Victor Hugo who placed the beginning of his famous novel Les Misérables there.
Museum of the Haute-Provence geological reserve and its butterfly garden.
Gassendi Museum with modern museography allowing the public to move from art to science, from ancient to contemporary through a journey through time. Its archeology section was founded in 1889.
World War II Museum. Documents and period objects evoke the strategic role of Digne-les-Bains in Alpine defense.
Alexandra David-Néel Museum, located in her house.

**Digne-les-Bains** (French pronunciation:[[diɲ le bɛ̃]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")ⓘ; Occitan: _Dinha dei Banhs_), or simply and historically **Digne** (_Dinha_ in the classical norm or _Digno_ in the Mistralian norm), is the prefecture of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provencedepartment in the [Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provence-Alpes-C%C3%B4te_d'Azur "Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur")region of southern France. Its inhabitants are called _Dignois_ (masculine) and _Dignoises_ (feminine).
Digne-les-Bains and neighboring municipalities
Located on the edge of the Digne Prealps and on both sides of the river Bléone, which flows southwest through the middle of the commune and crosses the town; it forms part of the commune's northeastern and southwestern borders.
Digne-les-Bains is the capital of the Department of Alpes de Haute-Provence. Placed in the geographical centre of the Department, the commune is home to 17,400 inhabitants, making it one of the smaller prefectures of France by its population. The town centre is at 608 metres (1,995 ft) altitude.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-LaTorre-3)

Digne is a sprawling commune in the plain formed around the Bléone Valley, given that the terrain that surrounds it is very rugged. The old town is built on a hill between the Bléone and the torrent of the hot springs, but the town has gradually extended in the three directions of the valleys, especially downstream. Its geographical location is quite remarkable, given that it lies at the edge of the Prealps, on a thrust fault that bears its name. A part of the town is completely enclosed in the Bléone Valley, while the town extends widely, on a gentler relief, downstream. With the annexation of neighbouring towns, especially downstream, the town extends over 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) in length.

### Neighbouring communes
[edit]
The communes surrounding Digne-les-Bains are La Robine-sur-Galabre, Le Brusquet, Marcoux, Archail, Tartonne, Clumanc, Chaudon-Norante, Châteauredon, Le Chaffaut-Saint-Jurson, Aiglun, Champtercier and Thoard.
Digne-les-Bains features a mid-latitude humid subtropical climate (Köppen climate classification: _Cfa_), with mediterranean (_Csa_) and oceanic (_Cfb_) influences. Summers are hot and relatively dry, and winters are mildly cold and relatively wet, with air frosts being regular in the winter months.

### Geology and terrain
[edit]
The commune, which is at the heart of the geology, has its specificities related to the ancient town _[clarification needed_] built upstream of the cluse which the Bléone has worn into the _Nappe de Digne_ to emerge into the tertiary basin of Valensole.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5)
The districts of the town cover the alluvium of the streams which converge upstream of the Cluse. The most eastern suburbs joined a line of limestone hills with flint of the Carixian age, forming russet cliffs oriented to the south-west.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5) The hot springs were captured, since ancient times, to the point where these carixian limestones are cut by the hack of the southernmost valley, descending from Entrages. Their healing powers are linked to their ascent along the gypsiferous Triassic levels of the sole thrust of the _Nappe de Digne_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5)
The most visible mountain of the commune is Le Cousson at 1,516 metres (4,974 ft); the Bigué rises to 1,653 metres (5,423 ft).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Brunet1-6)

**Tourism and main attractions**
Digne Cathedral is a Roman Catholic church. The cathedral has been a monument historique since 1906. It is the seat of the Bishops of Digne, Riez and **Sisteron**, formerly Bishops of Digne.
Construction began in 1490 by the order of the then bishop Antoine de Guiramand to cater for the movement of the town’s population to a higher, more secure and defensible location round the local castle. The cathedral was renovated and expanded in the 1860s under the direction of architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly.
The previous cathedral in the old town, Notre-Dame-du-Bourg (Cathédrale Notre-Dame-du-Bourg de Digne), a late Romanesque building of the 13th century, still stands as a museum.
The Saint-Jérôme de Digne Cathedral is the second cathedral in the city. Located in the heart of the city, on the Rochas hill, from the 16th century it replaced the original episcopal seat located at Notre-Dame-du-Bourg.
Antoine de Guiramand, bishop of Digne, from 1479, was behind the construction of Saint-Jérôme cathedral. The building, erected from 1490 to 1500, is the work of Antoine Brollion, master mason in Barcelonnette. Originally, it had a central nave of four bays flanked by side aisles onto which chapels were added during the 17th century.
The Notre-Dame-de-Lourdes Church was built in 1870 on the Mountain of the Cross, north of Digne, though at the bottom of the slope. The brick walls are its main feature, with its large size.
The chapel of Saint-Vincent belonged to an abbey or priory. It is still in good condition. The Chapel of the Cross, located nearby, is gradually becoming a ruin.

The remains of fortifications can be recognised if one pays attention to the plan of the old town around the central district, built on the heights. Some of the walls and some towers which surrounded the city from the 14th century can still be seen. These remains of ramparts are currently based in the landscape of the dwellings.
The town of Digne was immortalized by Victor Hugo who placed the beginning of his famous novel Les Misérables there.

Gassendi Museum with modern museography allowing the public to move from art to science, from ancient to contemporary through a journey through time. Its archeology section was founded in 1889.
World War II Museum. Documents and period objects evoke the strategic role of Digne-les-Bains in Alpine defense.
